question.problem: Calculate $L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ for the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{{6}^{n}}{{5}^{n}{n}^{6}}.$ According to the root test, does ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ converge or diverge?
question.worked_solution:
Suppose we have the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ such that ${a}_{n}\ge 0$ for all $n\ge 1,$ and that $L$ is defined as  

$$
L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n}.
$$

 

Then, the root test states the following:

- If $L<1$, the series converges.

- If $L>1$ or $L=\infty $, the series diverges.

- If $L=1$, the root test is inconclusive.

We have the sequence ${a}_{n},$ defined as

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{{6}^{n}}{{5}^{n}{n}^{6}}.
$$

To apply the root test, we find the limit of $\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{{6}^{n}}{{5}^{n}{n}^{6}})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }(\frac{6}{5\cdot \sqrt[n]{{n}^{6}}}) \\  & =\frac{6}{5}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{1}{\sqrt[n]{n}})}^{6} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\cdot {1}^{6} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the fact that

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{n}=1.
$$

Since $L=\frac{6}{5}>1,$ the series diverges by the root test.

choices.value: $L=1.$ The root test gives no conclusion.

responses.value: $L=1.$ The root test gives no conclusion.
